news.title: U.S. Treasury Yields Decline, Focus Turns to Jackson Hole
news.summary: U.S. Treasury yields declined slightly, hand in hand with oil prices, in early trade, as investors turned their attention to the Kansas City Federal Reserve's upcoming Jackson Hole symposium following Wednesday's key PCE inflation data.  "With core PCE holding at 3.3% year-on-year and the supercore re-accelerating, the pressure on [Fed Chairman Kevin] Warsh to signal a hawkish posture is real—but consensus remains that he will avoid a definitive policy commitment," Danske Bank's Jesper Fjarstedt said in a note.  The 10-year Treasury yield fell 1.2 basis points to 4.652%, while the 30-year yield was down 1.3 basis points at 5.171%, according to Tradeweb.
